## Computer Hardware

Every computer has a central processing unit (CPU) that executes instructions.

Types of CPU architectures:

- ARM (Raspberry Pi, Apple Silicon, Qualcomm Snapdragon)
- x86 (Intel/AMD CPUs)
- RISC-V

## Bluetooth Low-Energy (BLE)
Wireless communication designed for low-power, short-range communication.

What applications or use cases is BLE good for?

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
- Fitness trackers
- Healthcare devices
- Smart sensors
- Internet of Things (IoT) devices
:::

::: {.notes}
compare with bluetooth
:::

## Modes

Advertising: the device broadcasts its presence to nearby devices.

<br>

Connection: Bidirectional communication between central and peripheral devices.

## Services and Characteristics

Labels to organize BLE communication:

- Services: a group of related characteristics that provide a specific functionality.
- Characteristics: a single value that can be read or written by the central device.

## Profiles
BLE includes standard profiles that simplify development.

For example:

- Battery Service (0x180F)
    - Battery Level Characteristic (0x2A19)
- Heart Rate Service (0x180D)
    - Heart Rate Measurement Characteristic (0x2A37)

## Arduino
- Arduino is a microcontroller that allows you to control devices and process simple tasks 
- Can receive inputs and send outputs 

## Arduino
3.3 and 5 volt
- Provides power to circuit components and sensors 
GND 
- Reference point for current
- Current returns here
Analog Pins (A0-A5)
- Can be set as inputs or outputs 
- Used to read or send out signals 
- Can read or simulate a continuous range of values
## Arduino
Digital Pins(0-13)
- Can be set as inputs or outputs 
- Used to read or send out signals 
- Can only be on or off 
- Pins with a ~ can also act as analog output 
VIN 
- Input voltage pin used to power the circuit form an external source
USB port 
- Used to upload code, power the board and communicate with computer 
Restart button 
- Restarts the arduino program for the beginning

## Converting to Decimal (from non-Decimal)

1. Multiply each digit by its base raised to the power of its position (from
right to left, starting at 0).
2. Sum all the values obtained.

::: {.notes}
work through some examples with them
:::

## Converting to Binary (from Decimal)

1. Divide the decimal number by the base of the target system.
2. Write down the remainder.
3. Repeat the division with the quotient until the quotient becomes zero.
4. Read the remainders in reverse order (from last to first). This is the equivalent number in the target
base.

::: {.notes}
work through some examples with them
:::


## Bitwise Operators
```{.c}
// Bitwise operators: &, |, ^, ~, <<, >>
printf("  5 & 3  = %d  (0101 & 0011 = 0001)\n", 5 & 3);
printf("  5 | 3  = %d  (0101 | 0011 = 0111)\n", 5 | 3);
printf("  5 << 1 = %d  (left shift by 1)\n\n", 5 << 1);
```
